subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: What Anthropic server-tool contract should OpenClaw support for web_search, web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, and allowed_callers, and what opt-in, billing, replay, and security defaults must gate it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but provider-hosted code execution and delegated tool access can change tool availability, billing, transcript replay, container state, and execution boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
options.body: Add a narrow Anthropic plugin/provider contract for server tools, keep risky execution or billing paths default-off, and require docs plus live Anthropic proof.

options.title: Read-only tools first
options.body: Sponsor only native web_search/web_fetch first while keeping code_execution/PTC and allowed_callers behind a separate security decision.

options.title: Defer hosted execution
options.body: Keep this tracker open but reject code_execution/PTC until maintainers explicitly accept delegated provider execution as an OpenClaw capability.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Anthropic plugin/provider contract for server tools, keep risky execution or billing paths default-off, and require docs plus live Anthropic proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the latest visible review context and broad recent history across the affected Anthropic transport, config, plugin, and provider-boundary surfaces.
